key_idea: Gears only mesh within the same tooth size, and each size class contributes independently: pair largest with smallest counts, summing log ratios.
sketch: Group gears by tooth size s. Within a group sort tooth counts; each meshed pair (driver big, driven small) multiplies speed by big/small, and pairs from different groups chain through shared axles, so the total is the product of all pair ratios. Maximising the product means the top floor(k/2) counts go in numerators and the bottom floor(k/2) in denominators (the middle one is unused when k is odd). Sum log(big)-log(small). O(n log n). Pitfalls: n=0 gives 0; accumulate logs rather than the product.
